title: Things I Like
text:
Software

Files and folders


WizTree
Scans entire directories, folders and subfolders, and shows a treemap of where files are taking up space, among other things. I used to recommend TreeSize Free, but WizTree is faster and doesn’t push the paid version as much.


Path Length Checker deadlydog on GitHub
A stand-alone app that lists the path and length of every file and directory in a folder. Handy for tracking down Windows paths that are too long for some programs to handle.


Beyond Compare
File and folder comparison: versions by date or folder, folder structure, and line-level differences in text files. It also syncs one folder to another.


7-Zip
Unzips files, with more options than the standard Windows unzip. Handy.




Windows utilities and automation


PowerToys Microsoft
Handy Windows utilities, e.g. Find My Mouse, Workspaces, PowerRename, and the Command Palette.


AutoHotkey
Automates keystrokes and repetitive tasks on Windows.

Save Time by Saving Keystrokes with AutoHotkey

ahkbook: the book for AutoHotkey





Browser extensions


OneTab
Collapses all your open tabs into one list you can restore later, which clears the tab bar and frees memory.

one-tab.com



Pushbullet
Sends links and files between your computer and your phone, and mirrors phone notifications to the desktop.

pushbullet.com



Zotero Connector
Saves references and PDFs from a web page straight into Zotero from the browser toolbar.

My favorite text editor, with so many fun tools.

A Markdown editor built for academic writing, with citation support.

Notes in plain Markdown files, linked together.

Free for work use

title: Research interests
text:
Measurement & psychometrics. How well we measure things drives everything downstream. I work on scale scoring and missing-data decisions (person-mean imputation, prorated scale scores, completeness thresholds), measurement invariance, and structural equation and item response models.
Privacy-preserving synthetic data. With NSWERS, I generate synthetic versions of large, longitudinal administrative datasets so researchers and policymakers can explore them without exposing individuals, and I evaluate how faithfully they reproduce the original data (tidysynthesis, syntheval).
Applied evaluation & public policy research. At the NEAR Center and the Public Policy Center, I support program evaluation and policy research for state agencies and community partners, from study design and survey methods through analysis and reporting.
Research data infrastructure. Documentation, variable lineage, and reproducible pipelines: the tooling that lets teams trust and reuse their data. This is where my software comes from.
Youth physical activity & exercise physiology. My dissertation examined youth sport participation and cognitive development, and the need for better measurement. Earlier work covered neuromuscular fatigue, high-intensity interval training, and physical performance testing. See publications.

Internal; not publicly released.

NSWERS Data Explorer & Pipeline Visualization 2025–present
Author, R / Shiny

Internal application for the Nebraska Statewide Workforce and Educational Reporting System data warehouse: locates which tables hold which variables, retrieves definitions, and traces data lineage back to the queries and source tables each variable depends on. title: Contact
text:
Short bio
For programs, introductions, and session chairs:

Amelia Miramonti, PhD, is a postdoctoral researcher at the Nebraska Evaluation and Research (NEAR) Center and adjunct faculty in the Department of Educational Psychology at the University of Nebraska–Lincoln. She also supports applied research for Nebraska state agencies and communities with the University of Nebraska Public Policy Center, and develops privacy-preserving synthetic datasets from administrative records with the Nebraska Statewide Workforce and Educational Reporting System (NSWERS). She holds an interdisciplinary PhD from the University of Nebraska–Lincoln (2025) that combined quantitative, qualitative, and psychometric methods with exercise physiology and nutrition, an MA in Quantitative, Qualitative, and Psychometric Methods from the same institution, and a BSc and MSc in sport and exercise science from the University of Central Florida. Her more than 30 peer-reviewed articles range from neuromuscular physiology, strength and conditioning, and sports nutrition to child nutrition and career psychology. Her current work pairs measurement and missing-data methods with practical R and Shiny tools for data documentation, cleaning, and reporting, and she teaches graduate courses in computer-assisted data analysis and survey methods.
